entities.intro: A just official who investigates corruption in the Asiatic Department.

chapters.situation: The Asiatic Department has barred Gandhi from the Transvaal Indian deputation to Chamberlain and told him to leave.
chapters.summary: Tyeb Sheth wants to boycott the deputation, but Gandhi persuades them to go with George Godfrey reading the memorial, which they do. Chamberlain tactfully remarks that a new face is better than the same one. Taunted that war service brought no reward, Gandhi says good action always bears fruit. He decides to stay and fight the Asiatic Department from the Transvaal, is enrolled in its Supreme Court without opposition, and opens an office in Johannesburg with Ritch's help.

updates.gandhi: Swallows the insult and sends a substitute to the deputation. Decides to settle in Johannesburg for the long fight, is enrolled in the Transvaal Supreme Court, and opens an office.
updates.tyeb: Protests that an insult to Gandhi is an insult to the whole community and wants to drop the deputation.
updates.georgegodfrey: Leads the Transvaal Indian deputation to Chamberlain in Gandhi's place.
updates.chamberlain: Receives the Transvaal deputation and glosses over Gandhi's exclusion.
updates.ritch: Helps Gandhi find office rooms in Johannesburg's legal quarter.
updates.asiaticdept: Formally excludes Gandhi from the deputation.
updates.johannesburg: Gandhi's new base from 1903: office in the legal quarter.
updates.boerwar: Some blame Gandhi for advising war service that won no reward; he does not regret it.

chapters.situation: Gandhi has set up a law office in Johannesburg to fight the Asiatic Department and expects to stay for years.
chapters.summary: Gandhi admits that until now his self-sacrifice was mixed with saving for the future. In Bombay he had let an American agent sell him a Rs. 10,000 life insurance policy, but he now feels it shows a lack of faith in God and takes self-reliance away from his family. Through Ritch he joins the theosophists in Johannesburg in daily religious discussion without becoming a member, and his criticism of their conduct leads him to look inward.

updates.gandhi: Regrets his life insurance policy and plans to bring his family to South Africa. Discusses religion daily with theosophists.
updates.ritch: A theosophist who brings Gandhi into Johannesburg's theosophical circle.
updates.laxmidas: Gandhi's insurance was meant to spare his brother the burden of supporting his family.
updates.theosophy: Close daily contact in Johannesburg. Gandhi admires their ideal of brotherhood and criticizes their failures to live up to it.
updates.insurance: Gandhi comes to see insurance as distrust of God.

chapters.situation: Through the theosophists, Gandhi is in daily religious discussion in Johannesburg and is rethinking his savings and life insurance.
chapters.summary: The theosophists treat Gandhi as an authority on Hinduism, and they read Raja Yoga, Patanjali and the Gita together. Gandhi memorizes Gita verses stuck on his bathroom wall, thirteen chapters in all, and the book becomes his 'dictionary of conduct'. Its ideas of non-possession and equability, read alongside the legal idea of a trustee, lead him to let his insurance lapse and tell his brother that future savings will go to the community. His brother breaks off contact, but on his deathbed writes a moving letter of apology.

updates.gandhi: Memorizes thirteen chapters of the Gita and adopts non-possession. Drops his life insurance and stops sending savings to his family.
updates.laxmidas: Breaks with Mohandas over his refusal to keep supporting the family. Near death he writes to apologize, entrusts his sons to him, and dies before he can sail to South Africa.
updates.revashankar: Asked to let the insurance policy lapse.
updates.gita: Becomes Gandhi's infallible guide. Aparigraha (non-possession) and samabhava (equability) grip him.
updates.insurance: Read with the legal idea of the trustee, non-possession means holding everything as a trust. The insurance policy is dropped.
updates.theosophy: The Seekers' Club reads Vivekananda's Raja Yoga, Patanjali and the Gita.
updates.simplicity: Gandhi widens 'family' to mean the whole community.

status.laxmidas: Estranged, later reconciled by letter before his death

chapters.situation: Gandhi has embraced the Gita's ideal of non-possession and is pouring his energy into causes such as vegetarianism.
chapters.summary: Gandhi supports a struggling Kuhne-inspired vegetarian restaurant run by a German. He then lends about £1,000 of his client Badri's deposit, with Badri's casual consent, to an extravagant theosophist lady's grand vegetarian restaurant. It is never repaid, and Gandhi makes good the loss himself. A friend gently scolds him for risking clients' trust money, and Gandhi sees he broke the Gita's teaching of acting without desire for results.

updates.gandhi: Loses about £1,000 on a failed vegetarian restaurant and repays his client himself. Friends call him 'Bhai' (brother).
updates.badri: Trusts Gandhi with his savings, saying 'I only know you'. Gandhi repays him the lost £1,000. He later joins the satyagraha and is jailed.
updates.diet: Gandhi spreads vegetarianism by example and by backing restaurants, sometimes unwisely.
updates.insurance: As a trustee of clients' money, Gandhi learns that reforming zeal must not exceed one's limits.

chapters.situation: Gandhi's simple life in Johannesburg is growing more austere and he increasingly distrusts medicines.
chapters.summary: Troubled by headaches and constipation, Gandhi drops breakfast on the example of a 'No Breakfast Association' and the headaches vanish. Just's 'Return to Nature' introduces him to mud packs on the abdomen, which cure the constipation, and he becomes a lifelong advocate of earth and water treatment. Writing from his sickbed, he argues that 999 of 1,000 illnesses need no drugs, while warning readers not to treat any book as gospel.

updates.gandhi: Gives up breakfast and cures himself with earth packs. Writes these chapters from a sickbed.
updates.pjmehta: Had treated Gandhi successfully for debility in Durban.
updates.just: His 'Return to Nature' teaches Gandhi earth treatment and the ideal of a fruit-and-nut diet.
updates.naturecure: Earth bandages on the abdomen and Kuhne baths. Gandhi says 999 cases in 1,000 need no drugs.

chapters.situation: Gandhi has taken up earth treatment and is experimenting with diet.
chapters.summary: Gandhi's widely read 'Guide to Health' argued that people need no milk, only sun-ripened fruit and nuts, which make self-restraint easy. He reveals that during the Kheda recruiting campaign in India he nearly died, could not recover without milk, and broke the spirit of his vow by taking goat's milk because he wanted to live to fight the Rowlatt Act. He warns readers not to give up milk on his account and asks anyone who knows a true substitute to tell him.

updates.gandhi: Looking ahead: in India he will nearly die and break the spirit of his milk vow by taking goat's milk.
updates.guidetohealth: Gandhi's most widely read booklet. He still holds its views but no longer practises them on milk.
updates.diet: Fruit and nuts are his ideal diet; milk is the great exception he could not keep.
updates.vows: Gandhi admits he kept the letter of his milk vow by taking goat's milk, and knew he was breaking its spirit.

chapters.situation: Settled in Johannesburg, Gandhi is collecting complaints about corrupt Asiatic Department officers who take £100 bribes for permits.
chapters.summary: Gandhi gathers evidence and takes it to the Police Commissioner, who arrests two officers; one is caught after fleeing. A white jury acquits both, which disgusts Gandhi with the law, but both are dismissed and the department is cleaned up. Gandhi bears them no ill will and does not oppose their getting municipal jobs. He states the principle 'hate the sin and not the sinner' and calls it the essence of ahimsa and satyagraha.

updates.gandhi: Exposes two corrupt Asiatic officers. They are acquitted but dismissed, and Gandhi then helps them find work.
updates.policecommissioner: Listens fairly, investigates, and arrests the officers despite expecting a white jury to acquit.
updates.asiaticdept: Two corrupt officers are dismissed and the department becomes 'comparatively clean'.
updates.ahimsa: 'Hate the sin and not the sinner.' Resist the system, not the person.
updates.racism: White juries will not convict whites of crimes against coloured people.
updates.law: Gandhi is disgusted that intellect can be 'prostituted for screening crime'.

status.asiaticdept: Cleaned up after two officers dismissed

chapters.situation: Gandhi has been describing how he treats people of every creed and community as family.
chapters.summary: Gandhi recalls 1898 in Durban, when his clerks lived with the family and he and Kasturbai emptied the clerks' chamber pots. Kasturbai balks at cleaning the pot of a Christian clerk born to 'untouchable' Panchama parents and carries it in tears. Demanding she do it cheerfully, Gandhi drags her to the gate to throw her out. She shames him by asking where she could possibly go, and he closes the gate. He calls himself a 'cruelly kind husband' and says they are now tried friends, with Kasturba always the victor through her endurance.

updates.gandhi: Recalls with shame dragging Kasturba to the gate in 1898. Says he is no longer her 'teacher' or an infatuated husband.
updates.kasturba: Refuses, then tearfully cleans a Panchama clerk's chamber pot, and confronts her husband: 'Have you no sense of shame?' Now his faithful nurse and 'tried friend'.
updates.panchama: A Christian clerk of 'untouchable' birth whose chamber pot causes the quarrel.
updates.untouchability: Kasturba's resistance to cleaning a Panchama's pot causes the worst quarrel of their marriage.
updates.brahmacharya: Gandhi links his former cruelty to seeing his wife as an object of lust, an idea that changed from 1900 and took shape in 1906.
updates.ahimsa: Gandhi says his compassion 'dried up' in that moment.

status.kasturba: Gandhi's 'tried friend' and nurse (as of writing)

chapters.situation: Gandhi has been telling of his household of Indian clerks; now he turns to the Europeans who lived with the family.
chapters.summary: Gandhi pauses to explain that he writes week by week 'as the Spirit moves' him, without diaries, and reflects that all autobiography is inadequate as history. He describes taking English friends, including the theosophist Herbert Kitchin, into his Durban home during the Boer War. They adopted Indian ways, though they often cost Kasturba bitter tears.

updates.gandhi: Explains how he writes the autobiography and why he keeps going. Opens his home to Europeans as family.
updates.kasturba: Weeps over the English guests her husband brings into the home.
updates.kitchin: Lives with Gandhi's family in Durban during the Boer War.
updates.jairamdas: Gandhi says that if writing the autobiography is wrong, Jairamdas and Swami Anand share the blame.
updates.anand: Shares the 'blame' for prompting the autobiography.
updates.truth: Gandhi reflects that any autobiography leaves things out, and wonders how much he may omit in the interests of truth.
updates.religion: Gandhi says his faith in God amounts to experience, though he has not seen Him.

chapters.situation: Gandhi's Johannesburg office is overwhelmed with legal and public work.
chapters.summary: Unsure whether a white woman would work for a coloured man, Gandhi hires Miss Dick, a young Scottish stenographer who becomes like a daughter. He gives her away in marriage, after which she becomes Mrs. Macdonald. Her successor, 17-year-old Sonja Schlesin, introduced by Kallenbach, is fearless, blunt and free of colour prejudice. She refuses more than £10 a month, and during the satyagraha she leads the movement almost alone while the leaders are in jail. Gokhale ranks her first among Gandhi's coworkers.

updates.gandhi: Hires European stenographers, who become family to him.
updates.dick: Joins at £17 10s, becomes like a daughter and handles thousands of pounds. Gandhi gives her away in marriage.
updates.schlesin: Joins at 17. Refuses more than £10 a month, saying she works 'because I like your ideals'. Will lead the movement single-handed when the leaders are jailed.
updates.gokhale: Later ranks Miss Schlesin first among Gandhi's coworkers for 'sacrifice, purity and fearlessness'.
updates.racism: Gandhi doubts whites will work for an Indian, and is proved wrong.

chapters.situation: Gandhi's Johannesburg office has grown with new European helpers, and Ritch has become his articled clerk.
chapters.summary: Madanjit proposes the weekly Indian Opinion, launched in 1904 in Gujarati, Hindi, Tamil and English with Mansukhlal Naazar as editor. Gandhi in practice writes the editorial columns and pours his savings into it, at times £75 a month. He drops the token Tamil and Hindi sections as a kind of deception. For ten years hardly an issue lacks his article. The paper becomes a mirror of his life, a school of self-restraint, and the indispensable voice of the coming satyagraha.

updates.gandhi: Effectively edits and funds Indian Opinion and writes for almost every issue until 1914. Journalism trains him in self-restraint.
updates.ritch: Leaves his firm to become Gandhi's articled clerk.
updates.madanjit: Proposes and launches Indian Opinion in 1904.
updates.naazar: First editor of Indian Opinion, but leaves the hard editorials to Gandhi.
updates.indianopinion: Launched in 1904; Gandhi drops the Hindi and Tamil sections. 'Satyagraha would probably have been impossible without' it.
updates.publicwork: 'The sole aim of journalism should be service.'

chapters.situation: Gandhi is now running Indian Opinion and his Johannesburg practice, and the Asiatic Department has been cleaned up.
chapters.summary: Gandhi compares South Africa's Indians, branded 'coolies' and confined to 'locations', with India's untouchables and Europe's Jews in ghettoes, calling it a nemesis for Hindu untouchability. The Johannesburg municipality neglects the overcrowded location and then uses its filth as a pretext to take it over. Gandhi represents about 70 tenants for compensation, loses only one case, and gives his fees to Indian Opinion and the poor. He grows close to the ex-indentured leaders Jairamsing and Badri, who call him 'Bhai'.

updates.gandhi: Wins 69 of 70 compensation cases for location tenants. Is known among Indians as 'Bhai'.
updates.abdulla: Was the first to call Gandhi 'bhai', brother, and the name spread.
updates.jairamsing: Leads the ex-indentured Indians' association and helps Gandhi greatly.
updates.badri: Close collaborator in the location cases; later prominent in satyagraha.
updates.indianopinion: Swallows about £1,600 of the location fees.
updates.location: Overcrowded and neglected by the municipality, which then expropriates it on grounds of insanitation.
updates.untouchability: Indians in South Africa have become 'the untouchables of South Africa', a nemesis for Hindus' own treatment of untouchables.
updates.racism: 'Coolie' in South Africa means what 'pariah' means in India.

chapters.situation: The Johannesburg municipality has taken over the Indian location but left the residents in place, now as neglected tenants in worsening squalor.
chapters.summary: Pneumonic plague breaks out at a nearby gold mine, and 23 sick Indian miners return to the location. Madanjit breaks into an empty house to shelter them and summons Gandhi, who cycles there and informs the Town Clerk. Dr. William Godfrey becomes their doctor and nurse. Gandhi brings in his four young clerks, who say 'Where you are, we will also be', but keeps Ritch, a family man, out of danger. They nurse all 23 through the night.

updates.gandhi: Nurses plague victims through the night with Dr. Godfrey and his clerks.
updates.madanjit: Breaks open a vacant house for the 23 plague patients and calls Gandhi.
updates.williamgodfrey: Rushes to act as doctor and nurse to the plague patients.
updates.kalyandas: Gandhi's young clerks volunteer to nurse plague patients at great risk.
updates.ritch: Kept out of the danger zone because of his large family; works outside it.
updates.plague: Pneumonic plague from a gold mine strikes 23 Indian miners in the Johannesburg location.
updates.nursing: A night nursing black plague patients.
updates.location: An empty house in the location becomes a makeshift plague ward.
